other/2026-09-18-owl-setup.title: Owl Setup
other/2026-09-18-owl-setup.content:
Getting on the owls
I emailed Unni and did this as a part of getting a UiO account. Taken from the Component Separation Course:
Once you have received a username and password for your UiO account, you should log in and check that everything works before the workshop. Here are some instructions:
First you need to set up two-factor authentication (2FA) as decribed here:
www.uio.no/english/services/it/username-password/2fa/help/enable-2fa-qr.html
After this, open a Linux terminal, and log in to the ITA login node:
ssh -l <your username> login.astro.uio.no
At this point, as long as you’re outside of the UiO internet/Wifi, you will be asked for a 2FA code, which you should now be able to do if you have set it up. After you have logged in to the login node, you can set up a ssh key pair (there are tons of guides for how to do this online, for example this: www.howtogeek.com/424510/how-to-create-and-install-ssh-keys-from-the-linux-shell/). Even with a key pair, however, you still need to give your 2FA code as long as you’re working remotely.
From the login node, you can then access the owl cluster. The owl cluster is a bunch of machines that have names like owlxx.uio.no, where xx is a number from 39 to 46 when you want enough memory for a large commander run.
ssh owlxx.uio.no
Now you should be logged in to the owl and you can set up a similar ssh-keypair here so that you don’t have to provide your personal password each time.
Compilers etc are available through the module system. To see what is available, type:
module avail
We dont have any queuing system on the nodes, just be polite :) You can get an overview over available owls to run on here:
astro-clusters.uio.no/
Setting up python
I followed this link to set up python. It didn’t work directly but with some AI troubleshooting it did. Ultimately, it added these lines to my .bashrc:
# >>> mamba initialize >>>
# !! Contents within this block are managed by 'mamba shell init' !!
export MAMBA_EXE='/mn/stornext/astro/local/mamba/bin/mamba';
export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX='/mn/stornext/astro/local/mamba';
__mamba_setup="$("$MAMBA_EXE" shell hook --shell bash --root-prefix "$MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX" 2> /dev/null)"
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    eval "$__mamba_setup"
else
    alias mamba="$MAMBA_EXE"  # Fallback on help from mamba activate
fi
unset __mamba_setup
# <<< mamba initialize <<<
 
mamba activate py312

other/2026-09-21-gpt-uio-setup.title: Getting GPT UiO setup with API Keys
other/2026-09-21-gpt-uio-setup.content:
Overview
The university provides a free AI service called GPT UiO. It’s not terribly good, but free is better than not free! Best of all, it can be incorporated into VSCode or other IDE platforms.
The service is described here : GPT UiO
There are dozens of models. From my quick digging, it seems that the best as of writing this are GLM 5.3 for coding and GPT 5.4 for general work. They also specify a security level on each model, not something I am too interested in personally but it is nice to not have all of my queries trace directly back to me.
To get API keys
By doing this, you can integrate the AI into VSCode or any other platform, providing easy access to scripts and directory search. For VSCode, it just shows up as another agent that can be chosen in the chat tab.
This service is described here getting API keys
Email gpt-drift@usit.uio.no and provide:

your UiO email/username,
state that you are requesting API keys
Explain what you plan to use them for

They will then give you access to the My API keys option in the dropdown menu available from clicking your name.
Integrating the API keys into VSCode
This only took a few minutes once the keys were issued:

Log in to gpt.uio.no, click your username in the top right, and open My API keys. Hit Generate new — note there are separate keys for yellow-data and red-data models. I made one for each but only use the yellow-data models anyways.
Click on the model you want and copy the Key, Base URL, and Model name it lists.
In VSCode, open the Chat tab, click the model picker dropdown, and choose Manage Models. Add a new OpenAI-compatible provider, give it a name like “GPT UiO (Yellow)”, and paste in the Base URL and Key.
Repeat step 3 with the red-data key if you also want the red-classified models.

After that, the models just show up in the chat tab dropdown as another agent choice (e.g. GPT UiO (Yellow) / gpt-5.4). The key acts like a password, so keep it out of any committed files.
